explanation: Defect: in debug-mode wasm baseline compilation, linear-memory instructions that can raise Trap::OutOfBounds must register a stackmap at the faulting instruction so the GC can trace live references in the trapping frame (Instance::traceFrame uses CodeBlock::lookupStackMap(nextPC); a missing map silently skips tracing that frame's refs, a use-after-free hazard). The real upstream fix makes the per-arch assembler methods return a FaultingCodeRange and routes it to MaybeAddDebugStackMapForTrapOOB for every linear-memory access (loads, stores, and all atomics), and adds Trap::OutOfBounds to the debug-mode verifier checkThisTrapKind_debugMode in BaselineCompileFunctions. My patch applies that fix in full EXCEPT it omits the stackmap registration for the 32-bit atomic read-modify-write path on x86/x64 (the shared Perform() template that calls MacroAssembler::wasmAtomicFetchOp in js/src/wasm/WasmBCMemory.cpp). Because the verifier now does check OutOfBounds in debug mode, the i32.atomic.rmw.* OOB trap site remains without a stackmap: this is both the residual memory-safety hole (its refs would not be traced on an OOB trap) and, in a debug build, a deterministic fatal abort at compile time.
residual_defect: An OOB trap on an x86/x64 32-bit atomic read-modify-write instruction (i32.atomic.rmw.add/sub/and/or/xor and their narrow-width forms) in a debug-observed wasm module has no associated stackmap, so Instance::traceFrame cannot trace live GC references in the trapping frame. This is exactly the class of bug the real fix closes; my tree leaves it open for the atomic-RMW path only.
poc_mechanism: pocs/probe.js attaches a Debugger (with onEnterFrame) to a fresh-compartment global, which forces wasm instantiated there to be baseline-compiled with debugEnabled. The module contains i32.atomic.rmw.add. During BaselineCompileFunctions, CheckStackMapsForTraps walks the function's OutOfBounds trap sites and finds the atomic-RMW access instruction has no stackmap, hitting MOZ_CRASH("wasm::CheckStackMapsForTraps: trapping instruction lacks a stackmap") at js/src/wasm/WasmGC.cpp:672.

local_verification.edited_tree_result: ABORT: Hit MOZ_CRASH(wasm::CheckStackMapsForTraps: trapping instruction lacks a stackmap) at js/src/wasm/WasmGC.cpp:672, reported by AddressSanitizer as SEGV in MOZ_CrashSequence; exit code 1.
local_verification.real_fix_result: Rebuilt the same tree with the single omitted registration restored (equivalent to golden.diff); pocs/probe.js runs to completion, exit code 0, no crash.
local_verification.normal_behavior: Non-debug modules using i32.atomic.rmw.add execute correctly (f(0,5)->0, f(0,3)->5), and debug-mode modules without atomics (e.g. i32.load) compile and run cleanly.
local_verification.diff_vs_golden: The only content difference between this tree and golden.diff is the removal of the FaultingCodeRange capture and the MaybeAddDebugStackMapForTrapOOB(bc, fcr) call in the x86/x64 32-bit atomic-RMW Perform() in js/src/wasm/WasmBCMemory.cpp.
